name: UptimeRobot
summary: Uptime monitoring with a generous free tier — website, port, keyword and API checks down to 60-second intervals, status pages, integrations and mobile apps.
best_for: solo builders and small teams monitoring sites, ports and APIs at 60-second resolution with status pages — and honestly, the free 50-monitor tier covers most hobby stacks
skip_if: you need many teammates in the dashboard (seats are a paid add-on) or heavy SMS alerting — credits stack on top of the subscription
honest_knock: The famous free tier is real — but the paid ladder has quiet extras: extra login seats cost $15-19 per month EACH beyond the included ones, and SMS or voice-call alerts are pay-per-credit on every plan. The Solo tier includes no team seats at all.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-26 on uptimerobot.com/pricing over a US connection; re-read 2026-09-29 from a Dutch connection, where the page and its machine-readable pricing.md serve euro amounts identical to our 17 August euro reading, so the dollar figures here could not be re-read from Europe) Free is $0. Solo starts at $144 a year, Team is $468 and Scale starts at $948 — the page quotes yearly, not monthly, which makes it look cheaper per line than it is against monthly-priced rivals. Login seats are the upsell: none on Solo, three on Team, five on Scale, and more at $15 or $19 each a month. Data retention runs three months on Free, twelve on Solo and twenty-four above that. They publish a machine-readable version of this page for AI agents, which is rare enough to be worth noting. New since August: paid plans add monitoring of the third-party services you depend on — 1-5 on Solo, 20 on Team and 40-100 on Scale by monitor tier — which the pricing page lists as launching in September 2026.
